findings.finding: Idempotent replay with a different slug creates a number/path mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Same fix as openai finding 4 — (run_id, slug) keying, loud error on mismatch.

findings.finding: .shipwright/locks/ may not exist on a fresh clone or after git clean.
findings.suggestion: mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) before opening lock/watermark.

findings.finding: A pruned-but-listed worktree in `git worktree list --porcelain` could crash the scan with FileNotFoundError.
findings.suggestion: Catch per-worktree (FileNotFoundError/OSError), skip with a warning, continue the scan.

findings.finding: "Same-machine" scope is imprecise: two independent clones of the same repo on one machine do NOT coordinate (only linked worktrees of ONE main root do).
findings.suggestion: Reword scope as "linked worktrees sharing one main repository root."

findings.finding: Timing window: state deleted AFTER a claim but BEFORE the agent writes the spec file leaves the number unrecoverable by folder-scan (no file exists yet to find) — a later allocation can reissue it.
findings.suggestion: Write the spec file at the returned path IMMEDIATELY, same step, no intervening actions; allocator fails closed rather than silently resetting to the folder-scan floor when state is missing/corrupt while other worktrees are active.

findings.finding: Degraded WORKTREE-LOCAL mode still completes an unsafe allocation by default.
findings.suggestion: Unresolvable main root is a failure by default, not a silent degrade.

findings.finding: Slug used raw in path construction (traversal risk); idempotent replay with a changed slug or a pre-existing unrelated target could overwrite.
findings.suggestion: Validate slug against a safe-filename allowlist before use; key idempotency on (run_id, slug), error loudly on mismatch.

findings.finding: Anti-ratchet regeneration ambiguity — if the guard test regenerates-then-compares, a same-run collision becomes "baseline" and the guard protects nothing.
findings.suggestion: Guard reads only the committed baseline file; regeneration is a separate, explicit, human-invoked command; pin that the guard imports nothing from the regen tool.

findings.finding: AC2/AC3 have no recorded evidence of the verification work.
findings.suggestion: Add a Repo Scout Evidence section citing the actual greps/reads performed.

findings.finding: Stated verification command misses the new test_mandated_reader_index_first.py.
findings.suggestion: Broaden the Verification runner command to name all three new test modules explicitly.

findings.finding: Marketplace-sync timing concern ("stale PR" if sync changes tracked content).
findings.suggestion: Reviewed, no change needed — update-marketplace.sh only refreshes the local runtime plugin cache outside this repo's git history; it does not modify or generate any committed file.

code.raw_excerpt:
Both blockers verified resolved.

## Verification

**1. Anti-ratchet cleared.** `sub-iterate-runner.md` is now **497 lines** — exactly the baseline pin (`current: 497`, `state: exception`, `adr: "ADR-119"`). `test_runner_doc_within_bloat_ceiling` asserts `lines <= 497`, so it passes at the boundary, and `anti_ratchet` compares against `current` the same way, so the pre-commit hook will not fire.

**2. Parity holds, byte-for-byte.** Diffed the two bullets by eye at `sub-iterate-runner.md:486-489` and `code-reviewer.md:260-263` — identical text, identical indentation, identical line breaks.

`code-reviewer.md` went 316 -> 312 lines, consistent with the same -4 trim; at limit 400 and absent from the baseline, it has ample headroom.

The trimmed wording still carries the correction that mattered - `adr` is `"ADR-NNN"`, explicitly not a spec-folder path - which is the whole point of finding 6. Dropping the longer explanation of why the two numbering identities differ is the right trade at zero headroom; the full rationale lives in the run's ADR and in `docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md:2859`.

## Final verdict: APPROVE

All six medium findings resolved, all low findings resolved except three deferrals explicitly accepted (`_entries()` double match - spec-compliance wins; `iter_adr_files()` extraction - correct call at 300/300; artifact-write-matrix row - no such row exists for the sibling artifact either). No security, performance, or change-sizing concerns. Net source change well under 100 LOC across three Python files, single coherent concern, no dead-code artifacts, no baseline ratchet.

Two things to carry into finalization, neither blocking:
- The background `shared/tests` run is the one remaining unknown - read the `N passed` line from the output file, not the return value.
- Two nits from the earlier pass are still open, both cosmetic: the miniplan stale path mention (now fixed), and `load()`'s `str(int(...))` normalization is last-wins if a baseline ever carried both "97" and "097" (accepted, documented).

Process reminder for after merge: this diff touches plugins/*/agents/, plugins/*/skills/, and shared/scripts/, none of which reach the runtime plugin cache on their own. Run bash scripts/update-marketplace.sh after push, then uv run scripts/check_plugin_cache_sync.py --strict.

doubt.disposition: shared/constitution.md ALWAYS rule: adversarial doubt-reviewer pass applies only to changes touching risky ground (stored-data migrations, concurrency, anything hard to undo). This diff is skill/agent prose plus a pure filesystem/JSON-read guard module and a regen CLI (durable_atomic_write, no partial-write hazard) — no migration, no concurrency, no irreversible operation. doubt-reviewer's own agent description names the same trigger set (migrations, async/concurrency, cross-plugin imports, irreversible ops); shared/scripts/lib is imported by many plugins already, so this is not a new cross-plugin coupling. Not due, so not_applicable rather than not_run.

findings.finding: The template that is now explicitly copied to a run-id-named ADR spec file still gives that file the heading `# ADR-XXX: ...`. This conflicts with AC4/F3’s requirement that new non-numeric spec files must not claim an `ADR-NNN` heading before release assigns a real number. A user following “fill every field” can turn this into a hand-guessed number, and the generated index will present it as an ADR-numbered entry.
findings.suggestion: Change the template heading to a non-numbered title, such as `# Bloat exception — ...`, and clarify that the bloat baseline’s `adr` field is the separately assigned `ADR-NNN` identity.

findings.finding: Two live audit-docstring instructions advertise `.shipwright/planning/adr/<run_id>-…`, whereas AC4 requires the sanitized form `<run_id_sanitized>-<slug>.md` and specifically identifies `sanitize_run_id_for_filename` as the naming mechanism. Raw run IDs need not be valid/safe filename fragments, so this is not merely terminology: audit guidance can direct an agent to create a filename that does not follow the required convention.
findings.suggestion: Replace both occurrences with `<run_id_sanitized>-<slug>.md` and state that the run ID must be processed through `sanitize_run_id_for_filename`, consistent with the runtime audit messages later in the file.

findings.finding: The AC1b guard claims to reject both complete-read promises and `ALL ... decisions` wording bound to `decision_log.md`, but `_PROMISES_COMPLETE_READ` only recognizes complete/entire/whole/full-read constructions. A regression such as `decision_log.md — ALL architectural decisions` without “read completely” would pass despite violating the explicitly required AC1b prohibition.
findings.suggestion: Add a second alternation matching `decision_log.md` within the required vicinity of `all ... decisions` (in either order), plus a mutation-style test case demonstrating that this historical wording fails.  Overall assessment: The core index-first and collision-baseline implementation is sound, but the shipped template still promotes an invalid pre-release ADR heading and two audit instructions do not use the required sanitized filename convention. Ship with these targeted fixes. SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
